# Mutation differential battery fixtures

Golden JSON dumps for chunk 3 of the reference-model parity testing plan
(`planning/ifcopenshell-ts/80-reference-parity-testing-plan.md`) — unlike
`test/fixtures/reference/`'s vendored real `.ifc` files, there is no "reference model" for
a mutation: each `<schema>/<scenario>.golden.json` here is the result of applying a
scripted sequence of `ifcopenshell.api.*` calls to a blank file via a real installed
`ifcopenshell-python`, generated by `tools/reference_mutation_python.py`. The exact
scenario (every operation, in order, with every literal parameter value) is specified in
that script's own docstring per scenario — it is the actual cross-language contract: a TS
replay must reproduce it exactly, not "something similar," for the diff to be meaningful.

Two determinism fixes baked into the golden-generation script, both required reading
before adding a new scenario or replaying an existing one from TS:

- **`GlobalId` values are hardcoded**, not left as the real API's own randomly-generated
  GUIDs — a live Python run and a live TS run of the identical scenario would otherwise
  never agree on a random value by chance. The TS replay must overwrite each created
  entity's `GlobalId` with the same fixed value immediately after creation.
- **`IfcOwnerHistory.LastModifiedDate`/`.CreationDate` are normalized to `0`** in the
  golden — these are real `time.time()`-at-creation-instant Unix timestamps with no
  override hook, inherently non-deterministic across two separate process runs. The TS
  replay must apply the identical `0`-normalization to its own dump before diffing.

Regenerate via (from a Python environment with `ifcopenshell-python` built/importable):

```
python3 tools/reference_mutation_python.py test/fixtures/mutations
```
